column2: Subsoil hardpans in the Irugur and Palladam red soils occur at 15-20 cm depth, restricting root penetration and causing severe moisture stress and Nitrogen/Zinc deficiency.
column3: Physical: Cross-plough with a heavy-duty chisel plough at 50 cm intervals to shatter the hardpan up to 45 cm depth. Chemical: Apply 25 kg/ha of Zinc Sulphate (ZnSO4) as a basal dose and split Nitrogen (Urea) applications to prevent leaching. Biological: Evenly spread 12.5 t/ha of Farmyard Manure (FYM) or composted coir pith to prevent the pan from reforming.

column2: Alkaline heavy clay soils (Vertisols like the Peelamedu series) cause severe surface crusting when wet and form wide cracks that tear roots when dry. High pH locks out nutrients.
column3: Physical: Construct lateral drainage channels and add sand/tank silt to improve capillary water movement and drainage. Chemical: Apply agricultural Gypsum (CaSO4.2H2O) to displace bound sodium from the clay, followed by leaching. Biological: Incorporate green manures like Daincha before sowing to release natural organic acids that lower soil pH.

column2: Alkaline soils (pH > 7.5) cause Phosphorus to chemically bind to Calcium, making it unavailable for early root development and limiting the activity of nitrogen-fixing nodular bacteria.
column3: Physical: Conduct early summer tillage to enhance soil oxidation. Chemical: Apply Single Super Phosphate (SSP) to provide a readily available source of both Phosphorus and Sulphur. Biological: Treat seeds with Rhizobium (to fix N) and apply Phosphate Solubilizing Bacteria (PSB) to the soil to break the Calcium-Phosphorus bonds organically.

column2: Intensive farming on highly calcareous soils causes severe nutrient immobilization, leading to 'Pencil point disease' (tapering of the trunk), yellowing fronds, hollow nuts, and button shedding.
column3: Physical: Dig circular trenches around the palm base to conserve moisture. Chemical/Biological: Soil application fails due to alkalinity, so administer 200 mL of TNAU Coconut Tonic directly into the root vascular system every six months to bypass the soil. Supplement the soil basin with composted coir pith treated with Pleurotus fungi to improve organic carbon.

column2: Continuous rice-rice cropping in Anaimalai and Noyyal river belts leads to 'fluffy paddy soils' with low bulk density, causing poor seedling anchorage and sinking of draught animals. Severe Zinc starvation is also prevalent.
column3: Physical: Compact the fluffy topsoil by passing a 400 kg stone roller or sand-filled oil drum over the semi-dry field eight times. Chemical: Apply Lime at 2 t/ha once every three years to stabilize the soil, and add ZnSO4-enriched fertilizers. Biological: Dip seedling roots in Azospirillum slurry before transplanting.
